A piece being animated toward a grid cell can bump against a wall without its follow animation being cancelled, which is impossible with `MoveX`, because a second value-mode tween on an owned channel cancels the first outright. Self-restoring: the offset follows a half-sine, so it is guaranteed to be back at zero when the tween ends, and it is released if the sequence is cancelled part-way.

```csharp
TweenSequence NudgeX(float x, float duration)
```

(Lite) Horizontal-only `Nudge`, the sideways bump.

```csharp
TweenSequence NudgeY(float y, float duration)
```

(Lite) Vertical-only `Nudge`, the impact drop.

```csharp
TweenSequence BackgroundColor(Color to, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.backgroundColor`.

```csharp
TweenSequence Value(float from, float to, float duration, Action<float> onValue)
```

(Lite) Animate a plain number from `from` to `to`, handing each frame's value to `onValue`. The one verb that writes nothing itself, it exists for everything a game HUD needs that is not a style property: a score counter rolling up, a health bar's backing value, a countdown, an audio duck. Composes with every modifier, so a rolling counter can spring: **Interruption.** A value tween has no style channel to own, so consecutive ones stack rather than supersede, two rolls at once will fight over the label. When the value can change again mid-roll (a score usually can), keep the handle and `Cancel` it before starting the next, and pass the currently-displayed value as `from`.`onValue`Called once per frame with the interpolated value. Must tolerate being called a single time at `from` and then cancelled.

```csharp
TweenSequence TextColor(Color to, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.color` (text/tint color).

```csharp
TweenSequence Width(float toPixels, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.width` (pixels). Layout-affecting: triggers a reflow each frame, costlier than transform verbs. Prefer `ScaleTo` where a visual size change suffices.

```csharp
TweenSequence Height(float toPixels, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.height` (pixels). Layout-affecting, see `Width`.

```csharp
TweenSequence Size(float toWidth, float toHeight, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate both `width` and `height` (pixels). Layout-affecting, see `Width`.

```csharp
TweenSequence Top(float toPixels, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.top` (pixels). Layout-affecting, see `Width`.

```csharp
TweenSequence Left(float toPixels, float duration)
```

(Lite) Animate `style.left` (pixels). Layout-affecting, see `Width`.

```csharp
TweenSequence From(float value)
```

(Lite) Start the most recent tween from `value` instead of from wherever the element currently is. **This is how you write an entrance.** Verbs animate to a value and read from the live one at start, so `Fade(1f, 0.3f)` on an element that is already opaque is a legitimate no-op, correct, and not what "fade in" means. Naming the start makes the intent explicit: The start value is written immediately, at build time, so there is no frame of the old value before the animation's first write. Skipped when the current motion mode would snap rather than play, where priming would itself be the flash. Value verbs only (Fade/Scale/MoveX/MoveY/Rotate/…); ignored by `SlideIn`, which already positions its own start, and by the vector and colour verbs. **Two consequences of writing the value early.** `Cancel` before the sequence dispatches leaves the element AT the start value, cancelling does not undo the prime, because `Cancel` leaves things where they are by design. And if another tween is already animating that channel it keeps writing until this one supersedes it, so the no-flash guarantee holds on an idle channel, not on a contested one.

```csharp
TweenSequence Ease(EaseFunction ease)
```

(Lite)

```csharp
TweenSequence Spring(SpringPreset preset)
```

Drive the most recent tween with a named spring instead of easing+duration. **The duration you passed to the verb is discarded.** A spring settles on its own physics, so `Fade(1f, 0.4f).Spring(SpringPreset.Gentle)` does not take 0.4s, it takes however long that spring takes. Pass `0f` to make that obvious to the next reader.

```csharp
TweenSequence Spring(SpringConfig config)
```

Drive the most recent tween with a custom spring. As with the preset overload, the verb's duration argument is discarded, the spring decides when it has settled.

```csharp
TweenSequence WithResponse(float response, float bounce = 0f)
```

Drive the most recent tween with a perceptual spring (`response` = period in seconds, `bounce` = arrival character); full model on `FromResponse`. Named distinctly from `Spring(...)` so the literal call `Spring(0)` can't become ambiguous with the enum overload.

```csharp
TweenSequence Delay(float seconds)
```

(Lite) Delay the most recent tween by `seconds` before it starts.

```csharp
TweenSequence Loop(LoopMode mode, int count = 0)
```

(Lite) Loop the most recent tween. `count` ≤ 0 loops forever.

```csharp
TweenSequence OnUpdate(Action onUpdate)
```

(Lite) Per-frame callback for the most recent tween.

```csharp
TweenSequence Then()
```

(Lite) Open a new sequential step. Tweens added after run once the current step finishes.

```csharp
TweenSequence OnComplete(Action onComplete)
```

(Lite) Callback fired when the whole sequence completes (not on cancel).

```csharp
TweenSequence OnSettled(Action<bool> onSettled)
```

(Lite) Fired when the sequence stops, whichever way it stopped.`true` if it completed naturally, `false` if it was cancelled or superseded. Same verdict the awaitable returns. **Prefer this to `OnComplete` for anything a user can see.** Cancel is not Complete: starting a new value-mode tween on the same element and channel supersedes the prior sequence, and `OnComplete` then never runs. That is correct, but it means a selection highlight, an enabled state, or a "now it's safe to repaint" step hung off `OnComplete` simply will not happen if the user interacted during the animation. The symptom is a UI that looks broken intermittently, with no error.

```csharp
TweenSequence IgnoreReducedMotion()
```

(Lite) Always animate this sequence even when `ReduceMotion` is on (e.g. an essential transition that must still play).

```csharp
bool IsActive
```

(Lite) True while the sequence is dispatched and still running.

```csharp
void Pause()
```

(Lite) Pause the sequence in place; resume later with `Resume`.

```csharp
void Resume()
```

(Lite) Resume a sequence paused with `Pause`.

```csharp
void Cancel()
```

(Lite) Stop immediately, leaving the target at its current values. No completion callback.

```csharp
Awaitable<bool>.Awaiter GetAwaiter()
```

(Lite) Makes the sequence directly awaitable.`bool completed = await element.Animate().Fade(1f, 0.3f);` Resumes on the main thread when the animation ends. The result mirrors `OnComplete` exactly.`true` when the sequence finished (OnComplete fired), `false` when it was cancelled or superseded, cancellation never throws, and the continuation can branch on the result instead of mistaking an interruption for completion (Cancel ≠ complete). Await a sequence once. Detaching the element resolves the await as `false` whether it happens mid-flight or in the same frame the sequence was built. Note: like OnComplete, an animation on an element that is never attached to a panel never starts and so never resolves, there is no detach to observe; `Cancel` resolves it immediately.

```csharp
Awaitable<bool> AsAwaitable()
```

(Lite) The sequence's end as an `Awaitable{T}` (see `GetAwaiter`). Allocated lazily on first call; already-ended sequences resolve immediately.

## Springs

### `SpringPreset` enum Pro

Named, hand-tuned spring feels exposed in the fluent API and inspector.

```csharp
Gentle
```



```csharp
Snappy
```



```csharp
Bouncy
```



### `SpringConfig` struct Pro

Physical spring parameters. Springs are the headline capability USS transitions and `experimental.animation` cannot express.

```csharp
float Stiffness
```

Restoring force toward the target. Higher = faster/tighter.

```csharp
float Damping
```

Velocity-proportional resistance. Higher = less bounce.

```csharp
float Mass
```

Inertia. Higher = slower, heavier feel.

```csharp
bool ClampOvershoot
```

When true the spring never overshoots the target: progress is clamped at 1 and the spring settles there. Opt in for layout channels (Width/Height/Size/Top/Left), where an overshoot means the box bounces past its final size and reflows on the way back. Note: the clamp is a hard arrival guarantee, a large relay-seeded velocity that would cross the target on its first step pins there immediately instead of carrying momentum through.

```csharp
SpringConfig(float stiffness, float damping, float mass = 1f)
```



```csharp
static SpringConfig From(SpringPreset preset)
```



```csharp
static SpringConfig FromResponse(float response, float bounce = 0f, float mass = 1f)
```

The perceptual spring model (iOS / Framer Motion): describe the feel, not the physics. `response` is the oscillation period in seconds, smaller = faster/snappier (0.15 = a quick control, 0.5 = a large panel). `bounce` is how springy the arrival is: 0 = smooth, no overshoot (critically damped); toward 1 = very bouncy; negative = overdamped (a flattened, viscous arrival). Maps analytically onto stiffness/damping.`k = m·(2π/response)²`, `c = (1−bounce)·2·√(k·m)`.

```csharp
SpringConfig WithClampOvershoot()
```

Copy of this config with `ClampOvershoot` enabled (fluent).

## Stagger

### `StaggerBuilder` class Pro

The builder `AnimateEach()` returns: the same verbs as an animation, played on every element of a list, each starting `Stagger(seconds)` after the previous one.

```csharp
StaggerBuilder Fade(float to, float duration)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder MoveX(float to, float duration)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder MoveY(float to, float duration)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder ScaleTo(float to, float duration)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder SlideIn(Edge edge, float duration, float distance = 48f)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder From(float value)
```

Start the most recent verb from `value` on every element, the staggered entrance idiom, and the reason most people reach for stagger in the first place. Every element primes at dispatch and then animates on its own offset, so a list cascades in from hidden rather than each item popping at full opacity. Without this the only way to write a staggered entrance was to set the inline style on every element by hand first, which is what the shipped sample had to do.

```csharp
StaggerBuilder Ease(EaseFunction ease)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Spring(SpringPreset preset)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Spring(SpringConfig config)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Delay(float seconds)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Loop(LoopMode mode, int count = 0)
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Then()
```



```csharp
StaggerBuilder Stagger(float secondsBetween)
```

Seconds between each element's start. `0` = all together (pure parallel).

```csharp
StaggerBuilder OnComplete(Action onComplete)
```

Fires once, after the last element's sequence completes.

### `Stagger` class Pro

Timing math for staggered groups, exposed so callers can schedule around one. A stagger does not take `duration` seconds, it takes `duration + (count - 1) * stagger`, because the last element has not started yet when the first one finishes. That means **a fixed per-element stagger makes the group's length scale with the collection**: the same code that spans 0.2 s over ten elements spans 0.9 s over forty. If anything is timed to happen after the group, a repaint, a state change, a second animation, it will be correct while you are testing with a small collection and wrong in production. Use `TotalDuration` to schedule after a group, or `StepForSpan` to pin the group's length regardless of how many elements it turns out to contain:

```csharp
static float TotalDuration(int count, float duration, float stagger)
```

Wall-clock seconds for a whole staggered group: the last element starts at `(count - 1) * stagger` and then runs for `duration`.

```csharp
static float StepForSpan(int count, float spanSeconds, float maxStep = float.PositiveInfinity)
```

The per-element stagger that spreads `count` elements over `spanSeconds` of start offsets, so the group's total length is `duration + spanSeconds` whatever the count.`maxStep`Upper bound on the gap between neighbours, so a small collection does not get an absurdly slow cascade just to fill the span. Defaults to unbounded.

## Transitions

### `Transition` struct Pro

A reusable enter/exit transition preset, fade, slide (from an `Edge`), scale, and their combinations. Build one with a factory and play it with the AnimateIn / AnimateOut / Show / Hide / SwapTo extensions (see `TransitionExtensions`). Easing or a spring is an optional refinement via `WithEase` / `WithSpring`. Springs + reusable presets are exactly what USS transitions can't express. This is a value type, modifiers return a copy.

```csharp
bool DoFade
```

Animate opacity (0↔1) as part of this transition.

```csharp
bool DoSlide
```

Animate a slide from `SlideEdge` over `SlideDistance`.

```csharp
Edge SlideEdge
```

Which edge the slide originates from (when `DoSlide`).

```csharp
float SlideDistance
```

How far (px) the element travels during the slide.

```csharp
bool DoScale
```

Animate uniform scale from `ScaleFrom` to 1 (in) / 1 to it (out).

```csharp
float ScaleFrom
```

The scale the element grows from on enter (e.g. 0.9 for a subtle pop).

```csharp
float Duration
```

Duration of the transition, in seconds.

```csharp
EaseFunction Ease
```

Easing for every component of the transition. Null ⇒ the engine default (OutCubic).

```csharp
bool UseSpring
```

When true, a physics spring drives the transition instead of `Ease`.

```csharp
SpringConfig Spring
```

The spring parameters used when `UseSpring` is set.

```csharp
static Transition Fade(float duration)
```

Opacity 0↔1.

```csharp
static Transition Slide(Edge edge, float duration, float distance = 48f)
```

Translate in from / out toward a screen edge.

```csharp
static Transition Scale(float duration, float from = 0.85f)
```

Scale between `from` and 1.

```csharp
static Transition SlideFade(Edge edge, float duration, float distance = 48f)
```

Slide + fade together, the classic panel entrance.

```csharp
static Transition ScaleFade(float duration, float from = 0.85f)
```

Scale + fade together.

```csharp
static Transition Crossfade(float duration)
```

Opacity swap for screen transitions (out and in overlap). Same shape as `Fade`.

```csharp
Transition WithEase(EaseFunction ease)
```

Use this easing (clears any spring).

```csharp
Transition WithSpring(SpringPreset preset)
```

Drive the transition with a named spring instead of easing.

```csharp
Transition WithSpring(SpringConfig config)
```

Drive the transition with a custom spring.

```csharp
Transition WithResponse(float response, float bounce = 0f)
```

Drive the transition with a perceptual spring (`response` = period in seconds, `bounce` = arrival character); full model on `FromResponse`.

```csharp
Transition WithDistance(float distance)
```

Override the slide distance in pixels.

### `TransitionExtensions` class Pro

Play `Transition` presets on elements: enter/exit (`AnimateIn`/ `AnimateOut`), display-aware `Show`/`Hide`, and a minimal screen swap (`SwapTo`).

```csharp
static TweenSequence AnimateIn(this VisualElement element, Transition t)
```

Animate the element from its hidden state to fully visible. The hidden "from" is primed synchronously (opacity 0 / scaled down / slid off-edge); the actual tween dispatches on the next scheduler tick, so there's no flash and the USS single-frame trap doesn't apply.

```csharp
static TweenSequence AnimateOut(this VisualElement element, Transition t)
```

Animate the element from visible to its hidden state (does not toggle display, see `Hide`).

```csharp
static TweenSequence Show(this VisualElement element, Transition t)
```

Set `display:flex`, then animate the element in.

```csharp
static TweenSequence Hide(this VisualElement element, Transition t)
```

Animate the element out, then set `display:none`, but only on natural completion (a cancelled hide leaves it shown, per the engine's Cancel ≠ complete rule).

```csharp
static void SwapTo(this VisualElement container, VisualElement target, Transition t)
```

Minimal screen swap: animate out every currently-shown sibling of `target` in `container`, and animate `target` in. With `Crossfade` the out/in overlap.

## Hover, press and focus

### `InteractionExtensions` class Pro

Entry points for declarative micro-interactions.

```csharp
static Interaction OnHover(this VisualElement element)
```

Animate on pointer hover (enter → active, leave → rest).

```csharp
static Interaction OnPress(this VisualElement element)
```

Animate while pressed (pointer down → active, up → rest).

```csharp
static Interaction OnFocus(this VisualElement element)
```

Animate on focus (focus → active, blur → rest).

### `Interaction` class Pro

A declarative hover / focus / press micro-interaction bound to a `VisualElement`: on activation it animates to an "active" look (e.g. scale 1.05), on release it settles back to the resting look. Driven by pointer/focus events, it is interruption-safe, each transition cancels the previous one and re-captures the current value, so rapid in/out never snaps. Created via `element.OnHover()` / `OnPress()` / `OnFocus()` (see `InteractionExtensions`):

```csharp
Interaction ScaleTo(float scale, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Scale to `scale` while active; settle back to rest on release.

```csharp
Interaction FadeTo(float opacity, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Fade to `opacity` while active; settle back to rest on release.

```csharp
Interaction RotateTo(float degrees, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Rotate to `degrees` while active; settle back to rest on release.

```csharp
Interaction BackgroundColorTo(Color color, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Tint `style.backgroundColor` while active; settle back to the resting colour on release. With `OffsetTo`, this is what a menu row actually needs: the surface lifts and the label slides. Scaling a full-width row instead grows its text with it, which is why scale-only interactions never looked right on lists.

```csharp
Interaction TextColorTo(Color color, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Tint `style.color` (text) while active; settle back on release.

```csharp
Interaction OffsetTo(float x, float y, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Translate by `x`, `y` pixels **relative to where the element was resting** when the interaction first fired, and slide back on release. Transform-only, so it never reflows the list around it.

```csharp
Interaction OffsetXTo(float x, float duration, EaseFunction ease = null)
```

Horizontal-only `OffsetTo`, the label-slide of a selected menu row.

```csharp
Interaction WithSpring(SpringPreset preset)
```

Drive this interaction with a spring instead of easing. Combined with the velocity relay, rapid hover in/out hands momentum across, no dead-stop.

```csharp
Interaction WithSpring(SpringConfig config)
```

Drive this interaction with a custom spring.

```csharp
Interaction WithResponse(float response, float bounce = 0f)
```

Drive this interaction with a perceptual spring (`response` = period in seconds, `bounce` = arrival character); full model on `FromResponse`.

### `InteractionTrigger` enum Pro

Which input state drives a micro-interaction.

```csharp
Hover
```



```csharp
Press
```



```csharp
Focus
```



## Named states

### `VariantExtensions` class Pro

### `VariantSet` class Pro

Framer-Motion-style named states for an element. Define states with `State`, then animate between them with `To`. Interruption-safe, a new `To` cancels the previous transition.

```csharp
VariantSet State(string name, Action<VariantState> build)
```

Define (or replace) a named state, configured via the `build` callback.

```csharp
TweenSequence To(string name)
```

Animate the element to the named state. Returns the sequence, or null if unknown.

### `VariantState` class Pro

One named visual state in a `VariantSet`, a target look (any of scale / opacity / translate / rotation / background color) plus its timing. Only the properties you set are animated.

## Settings and accessibility

### `MotionSettings` class Lite

Global Cascade settings. The headline one is `Mode`, wire it to the OS "reduce motion" accessibility setting (or a user toggle).`Reduced` keeps animation but calms it, `Crossfade` replaces movement with fades, `None` snaps instantly. Opt a single animation out with `element.Animate()…IgnoreReducedMotion()`.

```csharp
static MotionMode Mode
```

(Lite) The global motion accessibility mode (WCAG 2.3.3), see `MotionMode`. Applied per-channel when a sequence dispatches; opt a single essential animation out with `element.Animate()…IgnoreReducedMotion()`. Mode changes affect animations dispatched AFTER the change (in-flight animations keep their constraints).

```csharp
static bool ReduceMotion
```

(Lite)

```csharp
static MotionManifest Describe()
```

The machine-readable capability manifest, every verb + its required fields, the ease/spring/edge vocabularies, and the numeric ranges. One runtime source of truth that the JSON parser reads from and that generates the discoverable AI docs, so the parser, schema, and guide can't drift. Handy for an AI tool to introspect what Cascade can animate.

```csharp
static MotionStats Stats
```

(Lite) A read-only snapshot of live engine load (active runners/sequences/tweens + pooled tweens), for a debug HUD, a perf assertion, or confirming animations have stopped. Cheap and allocation-free.

### `MotionMode` enum Lite

Graded motion accessibility (WCAG 2.3.3 "Animation from Interactions"). Set via `Mode`; applied per-channel when a sequence dispatches.

```csharp
Full
```

(Lite) All animation plays as authored (default).

```csharp
Reduced
```

(Lite) Everything still animates, briefly and without bounce.

```csharp
Crossfade
```

(Lite) Vestibular-safe: positional motion (translate/scale/rotate/layout, and closure-mode verbs like SlideIn/MoveTo) snaps to its end state instantly; opacity animations play as authored, so every transition reads as a crossfade.

```csharp
None
```

(Lite) No animation at all: sequences snap to their end state and fire OnComplete immediately (the old `ReduceMotion = true` behavior).

### `MotionChannel` enum Lite

Which style property an engine-driven ("value-mode") tween animates, the identity used for velocity handoff, channel supersede, and per-channel cancel (`element.StopAnimations(MotionChannel.Opacity)`).

```csharp
Custom
```

(Lite) A closure-mode tween (SlideIn/MoveTo/colors/…): no channel identity, so it can't be targeted by a per-channel stop or participate in the velocity relay.

```csharp
Opacity
```

(Lite)

```csharp
TranslateX
```

(Lite)

```csharp
TranslateY
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Scale
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Rotate
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Width
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Height
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Top
```

(Lite)

```csharp
Left
```

(Lite)

### `MotionStats` struct Lite

A cheap, read-only snapshot of Cascade's live engine load, for a debug HUD, a perf test, or just confirming animations actually stop. Read it via `Stats`. Counting is O(active sequences) and allocation-free.

```csharp
readonly int ActiveRunners
```

(Lite) Panels (per `IPanel`) that currently have a running Cascade ticker.

```csharp
readonly int ActiveSequences
```

(Lite) Sequences currently animating across all panels.

```csharp
readonly int ActiveTweens
```

(Lite) Tweens being stepped this frame (the live tweens of each sequence's current step).

```csharp
readonly int PooledTweens
```

(Lite) Idle tweens sitting in the shared pool, ready to be reused without allocating.

## JSON sequences and presets

### `SequencePreset` class Pro

Declarative JSON round-trip for `SequencePreset`, a stable, constrained schema an external tool (an AI assistant, a code generator, a content pipeline) can emit to describe an animation, which Cascade then validates and plays. This is the "AI-first" front door: emitting constrained JSON is far more reliable for a language model than generating freeform C#. Format and copy-paste examples.md`. Machine-readable schema.schema.json`.

```csharp
TweenSequence Play(VisualElement element)
```

Build and start this sequence on `element`. Returns the handle.

```csharp
static SequencePreset FromJson(string json)
```

Parse a JSON sequence description into a runtime `SequencePreset` instance. Throws `ArgumentException` with a human-readable message on any invalid input, use `TryFromJson` in tooling/AI loops that want to recover and self-correct. JSON shape.`{ "steps": [ { "actions": [ { "verb": "...", ... } ] } ] }`, steps run in sequence, actions within a step run in parallel. Verbs: Fade, MoveX, MoveY, MoveTo, Scale, Rotate, SlideIn, BackgroundColor, TextColor, Width, Height, Size, Top, Left. Float verbs take `"to"`; MoveTo/Size take `"x"` and `"y"`; color verbs take `"color"` (e.g. `"#FF8800"`); SlideIn takes `"edge"` (Left/Right/Top/Bottom) and `"distance"`. Shared.`"duration"` (seconds), `"delay"`, and either `"ease"` (e.g. OutCubic, OutBack, Linear) or `"spring"` (Gentle/Snappy/Bouncy, which overrides ease). Full vocabulary and prompt→animation examples.md`.

```csharp
static bool TryFromJson(string json, out SequencePreset preset, out string error)
```

Non-throwing parse. On success, `preset` is a fresh instance and `error` is null. On failure, `preset` is null and `error` describes the problem (e.g. "step 0, action 1: verb 'Fade' requires a numeric \"to\"") so a generator can fix its output. For an AI/codegen self-correction loop that wants to branch on the failure and apply a fix, pre-check with `Validate`, which returns a structured `MotionError` (code + offending field path + nearest-name suggestion). Note: the returned preset is a `ScriptableObject` the caller owns, to just check validity in a loop without allocating, use `Validate`.

```csharp
static bool Validate(string json, out string error)
```

Validate JSON without allocating a preset, for tooling/AI loops that test candidate output before committing. Returns true if it would parse; on false, `error` says why (same messages as `TryFromJson`). For the machine-readable form (code + field path + suggestion) use `Validate`.

```csharp
static MotionError Validate(string json)
```

Validate JSON and return a structured `MotionError`, the self-correction entry point for AI/codegen loops. Returns `None` (whose `IsError` is false) when the JSON is valid; otherwise a struct carrying the `Code`, the offending `Path` (`steps[0].actions[1].to`), the human message, and a `Suggestion` (e.g. `"FadeIn" → "Fade"`), so the caller can apply the fix instead of guessing it. Allocates no preset.

```csharp
static TweenSequence PlayJson(VisualElement element, string json)
```

Parse + play a JSON sequence on `element` in one call (no asset needed). Throws on invalid JSON; catch or pre-validate with `Validate`.

```csharp
string ToJson(bool pretty = true)
```

Serialize this preset to the same JSON schema `FromJson` accepts. Round-trips.`FromJson(p.ToJson())` reproduces an equivalent preset (numbers preserved to 6 decimals). Emits only the fields each verb uses; null actions are skipped (matching playback).

```csharp
static List<MotionAdvice> Lint(string json)
```

Report actions that are valid but inert, the companion to `Validate` in an AI/codegen loop. **Why this exists.** Verbs animate to a value and read from the live one, so `{"verb":"Fade","to":1}` on a visible element is a legitimate no-op. It parses. It validates. It does nothing. A generator told only "MotionError.None" has no way to learn that its entrance never appeared, measured on this package's own documentation, six of fourteen shipped examples had exactly this defect and four did nothing whatsoever. Advisory, never fatal: an element genuinely hidden by USS is a real case, and `Validate` keeps answering only "will this parse and run". Returns an empty list for valid-and-sensible JSON, and also for JSON that does not parse, linting is a second opinion on something already valid, so check `Validate` first.

```csharp
List<MotionAdvice> Lint()
```

Lint an authored preset, the same check the JSON path gets, for the inspector.

```csharp
static string LintSummary(string json)
```

Every advisory on one line, or `null` when there is nothing to say, the shape a console warning or an AI's next prompt wants.

### `MotionError` struct Pro

A structured validation failure from the JSON front door, returned by `Validate` (which gives `None` when the JSON is valid). The `Code` lets a generator branch, `Path` points at the exact offending field (`steps[0].actions[1].to`), and `Suggestion` offers a nearest-name fix (`"FadeIn" → "Fade"`), turning "guess the fix" into "apply the fix". The `out string` overloads of `TryFromJson` and `Validate` return just the `Message`.

```csharp
readonly MotionErrorCode Code
```

Machine-readable failure category.

```csharp
readonly string Path
```

Dotted/indexed path to the offending field.`steps[0].actions[1].to`. Empty for a whole-document failure (empty/invalid JSON).

```csharp
readonly string Message
```

The same human-readable text the string-returning overloads produce.

```csharp
readonly string Suggestion
```

Nearest valid name for an unknown enum value (verb/ease/spring/edge), or null.

```csharp
MotionError(MotionErrorCode code, string path, string message, string suggestion = null)
```



```csharp
bool IsError
```

True when this represents a real failure (any code other than `None`).

```csharp
static MotionError None
```

The "no error" value.

### `MotionErrorCode` enum Pro

A machine-readable category for a JSON-sequence validation failure. Pairs with the human message so an AI/codegen loop can branch on the failure instead of regex-ing a string.

```csharp
None
```

No error (default).

```csharp
EmptyJson
```

The input was null/empty/whitespace.

```csharp
InvalidJson
```

The text wasn't valid JSON, or the root wasn't an object with a "steps" array.

```csharp
MissingField
```

A required field for the verb was absent (e.g. a float verb with no "to").

```csharp
UnknownVerb
```

The "verb" value isn't a known `MotionVerb`.

```csharp
UnknownEase
```

The "ease" value isn't a known `EaseKind`.

```csharp
UnknownSpring
```

The "spring" value isn't a known `SpringPreset`.

```csharp
UnknownEdge
```

The "edge" value isn't a known `Edge`.

```csharp
NotFinite
```

A numeric field was NaN or Infinity.

```csharp
OutOfRange
```

A numeric field was finite but outside its allowed range (e.g. duration > 600s).

```csharp
InvalidColor
```

A "color" string couldn't be parsed.

### `MotionAdvice` struct Pro

One thing a linter noticed about a sequence that is nonetheless **valid**. Advisory: the JSON parses, and it will run. It just may not do what whoever wrote it meant.

```csharp
readonly MotionAdviceCode Code
```

What kind of problem this is.

```csharp
readonly string Path
```

Where it is, in the same dotted form `Path` uses (`steps[0].actions[1]`), so a generator can address the exact action.

```csharp
readonly string Message
```

What is wrong, in a sentence.

```csharp
readonly string Suggestion
```

The concrete edit that would fix it, ready to apply.

```csharp
MotionAdvice(MotionAdviceCode code, string path, string message, string suggestion)
```



### `MotionAdviceCode` enum Pro

Kinds of advisory `Lint` can report.

```csharp
None
```

No advice, the zero value, so `default(MotionAdvice)` is meaningful. Matches `None`.

```csharp
NoOpAction
```

The action will run and change nothing: its target equals the property's natural resting value, no earlier action in the sequence moved that channel, and it names no `from`. Overwhelmingly this is an entrance that forgot to say where it starts.

```csharp
DurationIgnored
```

The action sets both `duration` and `spring`. A spring is driven by its own physics and never reads the duration, so the number is inert, and reads as if it controlled the timing, which is the misunderstanding worth catching.

```csharp
FieldIgnored
```

A `"from"` on a verb with no float target (`SlideIn`, `MoveTo`, `Size`, the colour verbs). It parses and is then discarded, which for a self-correcting API is worse than rejecting it.

### `TransitionPreset` class Pro

An asset (Create ▸ Cascade ▸ Transition Preset) holding an enter/exit transition for the UI Animator component or for code: `preset.ToTransition()`.

```csharp
bool fade
```



```csharp
bool slide
```



```csharp
Edge slideEdge
```



```csharp
float slideDistance
```



```csharp
bool scale
```



```csharp
float scaleFrom
```



```csharp
float duration
```



```csharp
bool useSpring
```



```csharp
EaseKind ease
```



```csharp
SpringPreset spring
```



```csharp
Transition ToTransition()
```

Build the runtime `Transition` this preset describes.

### `InteractionPreset` class Pro

An asset (Create ▸ Cascade ▸ Interaction Preset) holding a hover, press or focus look for the UI Animator component or for code: `preset.Apply(element, trigger)`.

```csharp

```

Bind this preset's look to `element` for the given trigger.

## Effects

### `DropShadowElement` class Pro

A soft drop shadow or outer glow drawn with a mesh: no shaders, works in any render pipeline. Put the element you want shadowed inside it as a child. For a glow, set both offsets to 0 and use a bright color with more spread. Usable from UXML as `<Cascade.DropShadowElement>`.

```csharp
Color shadowColor
```



```csharp
float blur
```



```csharp
float spread
```



```csharp
float offsetX
```



```csharp
float offsetY
```



```csharp
DropShadowElement()
```



### `FilterEffects` class Pro

Animated USS `filter` effects, `BlurTo` and `TintTo` as fluent verbs on Unity 6.3+ (where UI Toolkit ships the filter pipeline). Opt-in and measured: a filter repaints the element through a post-processing pass every frame it animates, profile on target hardware. On older Unity versions the verbs compile but no-op with a one-time warning, so shared code stays portable. Coexists with (does not replace) the mesh-based `DropShadowElement`; backdrop blur is intentionally NOT offered.

```csharp
static TweenSequence BlurTo(this TweenSequence seq, float toRadius, float duration)
```

Animate a `filter: blur()` radius (px) to `toRadius` over `duration` seconds. Captures the current radius at start (0 if none); other filter functions already on the element are preserved.

```csharp
static TweenSequence TintTo(this TweenSequence seq, Color to, float duration)
```

Animate a `filter: tint()` color to `to` over `duration` seconds. Captures the current tint at start (white = identity); other filter functions already on the element are preserved.

---

# Cascade FAQ: Unity UI Toolkit animation library questions
Source: https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/faq.html

### Which Unity versions does Cascade support?

Unity 6000.0 and later. Each release is tested on the oldest supported version and on a current one. Animated blur and tint need Unity 6.3 or later; on older versions those two verbs do nothing.

### Does it work with uGUI (Canvas)?

No. Cascade animates UI Toolkit `VisualElement`s only (UXML/USS, also called UIElements).

### Does it work in the editor UI or only at runtime?

It's built for runtime UI: game menus, HUDs and app screens rendered by a `UIDocument`. The UI Animator component (Pro) also previews in edit mode.

### What's the difference between Lite and Pro?

Lite is the free tween engine: every verb, easing, sequencing, loops, await and reduced motion. Pro adds springs, stagger, enter/exit and screen transitions, hover/press/focus, named states, the no-code UI Animator, JSON sequences, and shadow/glow. See the [table on the overview](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/index.html).

### How do I upgrade from Lite to Pro?

Remove Cascade Lite, then install Cascade Pro. Pro contains everything in Lite with the same namespace and calls, so your code keeps compiling. Don't install both at once.

### What's the license?

Cascade Lite is MIT licensed. Cascade Pro uses the standard Unity Asset Store license.

### Which platforms?

All platforms UI Toolkit supports. Cascade is pure C# with no native code and no dependencies.

### Why not just use USS transitions?

Use them for hover colors and simple toggles. They can't run steps in order, stagger a list, await the end, or spring. [How to animate a VisualElement](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/animate-visualelement.html) compares the options.

### Does it allocate every frame?

No. Tweens are pooled and the update loop is allocation-free; the test suite measures it. See [Performance and lifecycle](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/performance.html).

### Does it keep animating when the game is paused?

Yes. Cascade runs on unscaled time, so a pause menu animates with `Time.timeScale = 0`.

### My fade-in does nothing. Why?

The element is already at full opacity, so it fades from 1 to 1. Add `.From(0f)`. More in [Common mistakes](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/recipes.html#common-mistakes).

### Can an AI assistant write Cascade code?

Yes. Install the agent skill with `npx skills add twitchedd/cascade-skill`. See [AI assistants and the skill](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/ai-and-skill.html).

### Where do I get help or report a bug?

Use the contact options on the [twitched site](https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/../../) or the publisher page on the Unity Asset Store. Include your Unity version, the tier, and the smallest code that shows the problem.

---

# Cascade changelog: what's new in each release of the Unity UI Toolkit animation library
Source: https://twitchedd.github.io/cascade/docs/changelog.html

What changed in each release, newest first. Lite and Pro share one version number and ship together. Items marked Pro are only in Pro; everything else is in both.

To update, open Package Manager, select Cascade under My Assets and click Update. The full changelog also ships inside the package as `CHANGELOG.md`.

## 1.2.1 (2026-11-14)

### Changed

- **Clearer guidance for AI coding assistants.** The AI guide and the rules written by **Tools > Cascade > Set Up AI Assistants** Pro now explain three things that misled assistants: `Loop()` repeats only the verb right before it, never a `Then()` chain; `Delay()` delays the verb before it, so a `Delay` before any verb does nothing; and the stagger example used an `AnimateEach` overload that doesn't exist.
- **A shorter, code-first AI guide.** `AI-GUIDE.md` is a little over half its old size and has a new "Behaviour and exact names" section: which animations replace a running one, when `From()` applies, `OnComplete` vs `OnSettled`, counting a number with `Value()`, and the exact ease and verb names. The JSON sequence format moved to its own file, `AI-GUIDE-JSON.md`. Assistants get Cascade code right first time more often and spend fewer tokens doing it.
- The `Loop()` documentation comment (what your IDE shows) now says it loops only the most recent verb.

After upgrading, run **Set Up AI Assistants** again to refresh the rules in your project.

## 1.2.0 (2026-11-11)

### Added

- **Juice verbs.** `Shake(strength, duration)` and `Punch(offset, duration)` in both tiers; in Pro also a tunable `Shake` (vibrato, decay, axis), `PunchScale`, `PunchRotate`, `Pulse`, `Wiggle` and `Pop`. They start and end at rest, layer on top of a running move or scale instead of cancelling it, and put the element back if cancelled. Under reduced motion they skip straight to rest.
- **`At(seconds)`**: place the verbs that follow at a time from the start of the sequence while the `Then()` chain carries on, all under one handle.
- **Style verbs:** `BorderRadius`, `BorderWidth`, `BorderColor`, `FontSize`, `Padding`, `Tint`, `Right` and `Bottom`, with matching `MotionChannel` values for `StopAnimations(channel)`.
- **`WithVelocity(unitsPerSecond)`** Pro: start a spring already moving, so a thrown card keeps the speed of the drag as it springs home.
- **Code checks:** an analyzer in the Unity console and your IDE that warns about animation code that compiles but doesn't do what was meant (CASC001 to CASC008), such as a duration in milliseconds or an entrance with no start value.
- **Tools > Cascade > Set Up AI Assistants** Pro: writes Cascade's rules into AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Copilot and Cursor files, keeping their existing content.
- A "juice & timing" section in the gallery sample, and keyboard navigation for the gallery's section rail.

### Changed

- Pro Three showcase samples redesigned: the Starfall Combat HUD, the Pocket Shop (now The Gilded Anvil, a medieval shop) and Mission Control (now a SaaS dashboard with a command palette).

### Fixed

- The JSON schema and the inspector treated `Nudge` as a from/to verb; it takes an x/y offset.
- A Lite gallery example faded in without `.From(0f)`, so copied on its own it did nothing.

## 1.1.0 (2026-10-14)

### Added

- Pro Four showcase samples: Mission Control Dashboard, Starfall Combat HUD, Pocket Shop and Afterhours Audio Studio, each a complete animated UI Toolkit screen.
- Links to these online docs from Package Manager, the README and the getting-started guide.

### Fixed

- The documentation files and sample READMEs could be missing from the Asset Store download.
- Lite: assembly references to `Cascade.Lite.Runtime` broke on every update.
- Lite: the AI guide's fade-in examples omitted `.From(0f)`, so they did nothing on a visible element.

## 1.0.1 (2026-10-02)

### Fixed

- A compile error (`CS0619`) in the UI Animator inspector on newer Unity 6 editors.

## 1.0.0 (2026-08-25)

First public release: the tween engine with fades, moves, scales, rotation, colors and sizes, the full easing set, sequencing, loops, `await`, `Value()` for plain numbers, `OnSettled` and reduced motion. Pro adds springs, stagger, enter/exit and screen transitions, hover/press/focus animations, named states, the no-code UI Animator, JSON sequences and shadow/glow.
